badge: FOR WE THE PEOPLE OF INDIA
heading: Why The Constitution Matters
subheading: Adopted on 26th November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly, the Constitution of India is a sacred social covenant protecting 1.47 billion citizens from arbitrary power.

intro.para1: The Constitution is more than a legal document. It is a solemn promise that no person, institution or government is above the law; that power must remain accountable and that the dignity and rights of every individual must be respected.
intro.para2: It protects citizens from arbitrary exercise of power and provides peaceful, constitutional means to question authority, seek justice and defend our freedom. The Constitution belongs to "We, the People of India."

essay.label: NATIONAL IMPERATIVE
essay.title: Why Should We Protect the Constitution?
essay.para1: Freedom is never lost in a single day. It is weakened gradually. When constitutional values are compromised, institutions lose their independence and rights cease to receive equal protection. The Constitution of India is the foundation of our democratic Republic. It guarantees justice, liberty, equality and dignity, protects fundamental rights and establishes the rule of law. It also provides the constitutional framework for secularism, federalism and democratic governance.
essay.para2: Today, concerns are being raised about the weakening of these safeguards, including institutional independence, freedom of expression, equality before the law, cooperative federalism and the rights of minorities.
essay.para3: When constitutional protections are weakened, the impact goes beyond any one community or political group. The erosion of a particular person's rights ultimately weakens the security of everyone's rights. Public trust declines, institutions lose credibility and the constitutional limits on power are becoming increasingly fragile.
essay.para4: India's greatest strength is its diversity. The Constitution provides the common ground on which people of different faiths, languages, castes, genders and regions can live as equals.
essay.para5: Protecting the Constitution is therefore not merely the duty of courts, legislatures or governments. It is a shared responsibility of every citizen.
